Three-Tier Model

Model Tier by Data Volume — Not by Plan

Tier is determined by your tenant's own churn history, not your subscription. No tenant is forced into a learned model they can't support.

Insufficient history

Heuristic

< 30 churn events

Hand-weighted formula (6 components)

Asserted weights: subscription 30 / financial 22 / engagement 17 / NPS 10 / onboarding 6 / support 15. No training data required. Serves as cold-start for every tenant.

"Health score = 72/100 — "Heuristic — insufficient history""

Censored handled correctly

Statistical

30–200 churn events

Cox proportional hazards / Kaplan-Meier

Survival analysis handles censored observations — customers who haven't churned yet are information, not missing data. Works at genuinely low n where classification fails.

Learned

> 200 churn events

LightGBM + isotonic calibration

Gradient-boosted trees, warm-started from public base model. Isotonic calibration + conformal prediction intervals. Capacity scales to tenant data size.

Intelligence Differentiators

Six Reasons This Isn't Another 'AI Feature'

Calibration, conformal, SHAP, isolation, monitoring, provenance — not marketing checkboxes, architectural guarantees.

Three-Tier Degradation

Heuristic → Statistical → Learned. Automatic fallback if calibration degrades (Brier score >20% worse or AUC >0.05 worse). Never serves confident nonsense.

Conformal Prediction Intervals

Distribution-free, valid at small n. Honest interval (69–77%) not a point estimate dressed as certainty. Coverage target 90%.

SHAP Explanations in Business Language

"Payment latency increased from 4 to 31 days" not "feature_12: 0.28". The explanation is the product; the probability is just the sort key.

Strict Per-Tenant Isolation

The scoring pipeline can never bypass tenant isolation, by design — not by convention. Standing test: the model for tenant A produces identical output whether tenant B's rows exist or not. DPDP 2023 compliant by architecture, not policy.

Calibration Monitoring Built-In

Brier score + reliability curve (10 bins) computed per training run. Reliability curve stored and surfaced in calibration dashboard. Active artifact swap on degradation.

UI Contract: Every Number Shows Provenance

Mode (heuristic/statistical/learned), confidence interval, sample size. No number appears without its provenance. Members see one number; managers see comparison.

ML Pipeline

Nightly Training. Detached Processes. EventBridge Triggered.

Follows the proven polynovea-payroll-compute pattern. EC2, not Lambda — once-daily job doesn't need on-demand elasticity.

1

Resolve Tier

Per tenant, count real churn events (backfilled=false). <30 → heuristic, 30–200 → statistical, >200 → learned.

2

Train Blended

Load public base model (public-cx-churn-v1), warm-start LightGBM on tenant data, isotonic calibrate, conformal intervals, SHAP.

3

Tenant-Only Audit

Optional, monthly. Only if audit switch ON AND >200 events. Trains from scratch, compares metrics vs blended.

4

Inference

Scores current orgs against active blended artifact. Writes entity_scores (churn_risk, computed_by=ml, model_run_id).

5

Calibration Check

New run Brier/AUC vs previous. If degraded → new artifact inactive, previous stays active. Fallback is automatic.

Visibility Split

Role-Gated Access — Real Roles, Not Invented Ones

Checked against actual role hierarchy (master_admin > admin > manager > member). No 'team lead' role that doesn't exist.

Member (Default CS Rep)

Sees ONE number — the production blended model's prediction, scoped to accounts they have access to. No model-selection UI, no comparison, just the answer and its SHAP explanation.

Single churn risk numberSHAP explanationConfidence intervalSample sizeTier badge (heuristic/statistical/learned)

Manager + (Admin, Master Admin)

Sees BOTH models and the comparison, for tenants where the audit switch is ON and volume floor (>200) is cleared. This is for deciding whether to flip the warm-start config flag.

Tenant Isolation

Structural Enforcement — Not a Code Convention

Cross-tenant ML pooling is permanently excluded (DPDP 2023). The rule is structural at every layer.

LayerEnforcement
QueryEvery training/inference query filters tenant_id = $1. Lambda receives exactly one tenantId per invocation — no code path iterates tenants.
DB RoleThe scoring service always connects through the restricted, tenant-scoped role — never an elevated one. A missing tenant filter returns zero rows, not everyone's data.
ArtifactsTrained models stored per tenant (model_artifacts.tenant_id NOT NULL). Never merged. Never used as initialization for another tenant.
Job Tableml_inference_jobs.tenant_id NOT NULL + RLS. A job is scoped to one tenant by construction.
VerificationStanding test: model trained for tenant A produces identical output whether tenant B rows exist or not. Runs on every deploy.

Accepted Trade-Off: Small Tenants Stay on Heuristic Longer

A tenant with 20 customers gets an honest "insufficient history" label rather than a confident prediction borrowed from someone else's business. This is the correct trade. Pooling would materially improve small-tenant accuracy, and that is exactly the pressure this rule exists to resist.
